statement: Dr. Irfan Ahmad Khan founded and directed the Association of Quranic Understanding.

conflict.resolution: Site style uses 'of', following Dr. Khan's own signatures and AQU newsletters. The 'for' variant appears in press, retail catalogs, and on at least one printed title page.

statement: Dr. Khan published three books in English.
Chapter 34 of An Exercise in Understanding the Qur'an is titled 'An Overall Look' and addresses the structural and thematic organization of surahs 85 through 114.
Dr. Khan completed a doctorate at the University of Illinois at Chicago in 1986 with a dissertation titled The Thing-Event Distinction.
Dr. Khan undertook advanced study in the Islamic sciences at a residential institution in Rampur, India, established following a proposal by Abul A'la Maududi for science graduates.
Dr. Khan relocated to the United States and settled in Chicago.
Dr. Khan held trustee roles with the Parliament of the World's Religions.

conflict.resolution: Both may be accurate at different periods. Dates not established.

statement: Dr. Khan was founding president of the Interreligious Engagement Project for the 21st Century.
Dr. Khan was founder and president of the World Council of Muslims for Interfaith Relations.
Dr. Khan is reported to have read the Qur'anic imperative concerning orphans as extending beyond fatherless children to disenfranchised populations generally.
Dr. Khan is reported to have compared Qur'anic critiques of earlier scriptural communities to the admonitions of the prophet Amos, arguing they address factions rather than whole communities.
Dr. Khan is reported to have chaired the Interfaith Committee of the Council of Islamic Organizations of Greater Chicago.
